references.text: Describes how God gave 'bread from heaven' (manna) to Israel in the wilderness, a direct precursor motif to Jesus declaring himself as the 'bread from heaven' that gives life.
Recalls God's gift of bread from heaven, creating a clear parallel to Jesus' claim to be the true bread coming down from heaven to give eternal life.
Moses explains that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word from God. This sets the stage for Jesus' claim to be the very bread (God's word/presence) that gives life.
Invites all who are thirsty to come and receive food without cost, a motif fulfilled by Jesus offering himself as the bread that satisfies spiritual hunger.
Jesus expands on the claim by saying that the bread he gives is his flesh, which will give the world life, thus linking 'the bread' directly to 'life' and his sacrifice.
